key_insight: Near-wall concentric airfoil grids can suppress turbulence enough to produce net drag reduction in a pipe, boosting flow rate by up to 9.0% at Re ≈ 10^5.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a passive flow-straightening design that could reduce pumping power in water and gas pipelines without the usual net-loss penalty of internal devices.
method: Axisymmetric RANS simulations with the k-ω SST turbulence model
Periodic boundary conditions in a pipe-flow configuration
Validated against fully developed turbulent pipe flow and prior large-eddy breakup device data
evidence_signal: At a pressure difference corresponding to Re ≈ 10^5, the best near-wall grid pattern increased flow rate by up to 9.0%, reduced area-integrated Reynolds shear stress by 29%, and stayed beneficial from 5×10^4 to 2×10^5.
watch_item: Results are based on RANS modeling, so experimental verification and sensitivity to real pipe roughness, fabrication tolerances, and pressure-loss penalties are important before deployment.
paper_title: Net drag reduction in turbulent pipe flow by airfoil-section grids concentrated near the wall
